issues.legal_issue: A transfer agreement is vitiated by fraud when a fiduciary conceals substantial accrued dividends from the person transferring the shares.
material_facts: The transferor assigned his remaining shares for consideration of 18,000 dollars.
The transferee had collected 35,535 dollars and 50 cents in dividends on the shares but concealed that fact from the transferor.
The transferee was under a fiduciary obligation to disclose the true state of affairs.

The courts below concurrently found that the agreement was vitiated by fraud; the contention that the transferor could have discovered the truth with ordinary diligence had not been raised in the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The finding that the transfer agreement was vitiated by fraud was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 19 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, fraud may make an agreement voidable; the court rejected the ordinary-diligence contention because it had not been raised in the High Court and was too late to raise on appeal. A fiduciary must disclose material facts within the scope of that obligation, and concealment of the substantial dividends supported the concurrent finding of fraud.

predicates.appeal_challenges_fraud_finding: A party in an appeal challenges a finding that a transfer agreement was vitiated by fraud.
predicates.fiduciary_duty_to_disclose: The person receiving the transfer owed the transferor a fiduciary duty to disclose the relevant state of affairs.
predicates.material_dividends_concealed: The recipient concealed substantial dividends already collected on the transferred shares.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a fraud finding and the recipient owed a disclosure duty but concealed substantial collected dividends, the transfer agreement is vitiated by fraud.

issues.legal_issue: A defendant's absence from India is excluded when computing limitation for a suit in India even if the cause of action arose abroad and the defendant was abroad when it arose.
material_facts: The suit was brought in an Indian court that had jurisdiction and was governed by the Indian Limitation Act, 1908.
The cause of action arose in Malacca, where the defendant was also present when it arose.
The defendant was absent from India for periods after the cause of action accrued.
The suit was for relief on the ground of fraud, and the fraud was found to have been discovered in April 1924; the suit was filed in September 1927.
The parties accepted that excluding the defendant's absence from India made the suit timely.
issues.conclusion: The defendant's periods of absence from India had to be excluded under section 13, and the suit was not barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: Article 95 of the Indian Limitation Act, 1908 made the discovery of fraud the starting point for limitation. Section 13 required exclusion of time during which the defendant was absent from India and made no exception where the cause of action arose abroad or the defendant was abroad when it accrued. The Court applied Atul Kristo Bose v. Lyon & Co. and Mathukanni v. Andappa, and approved the latter's rejection of Ruthinu v. Packiriswami and Subramania Chettiar v. Maruthamuthu.

predicates.suit_in_indian_court_governed_by_indian_: A suit is brought in an Indian court with jurisdiction and is governed by Indian limitation law.
predicates.defendant_absent_from_india_during_limit: The defendant is outside India during a period relevant to computing limitation, whether or not the cause of action arose abroad or the defendant was abroad when it accrued.

issues.definition: For a suit in an Indian court governed by Indian limitation law, time when the defendant is absent from India is excluded from the limitation computation.

issues.legal_issue: The value of transferred shares for the monetary accounting must be assessed as of the date of transfer using the evidence of their value at that time.
material_facts: The High Court valued the shares as of the transfer date by relying on a later value and an asserted market trend.
The record contained evidence of actual share transfers at different prices, including transfers close to the date of the agreement.
The parties agreed that the shares should be valued as of the agreement date, and the Court assessed their value from the recorded transfer prices.
issues.conclusion: The High Court's share valuation was erroneous; the Supreme Court reassessed the value as of the agreement date and modified the decree accordingly.
issues.legal_principle: The value relevant to the accounting was the value of the shares on the date of transfer. The Court relied on the record of actual share transfers and the evidence of their prices rather than extrapolating from a later value and general market movement.

predicates.appeal_reviews_monetary_decree: An appeal asks the court to review a monetary decree that depends on valuing transferred shares.
predicates.shares_must_be_valued_at_transfer: The parties' accounting requires the shares to be valued as of the transfer date.
predicates.evidence_shows_market_prices_near_transf: The record contains evidence of actual share prices from transactions near the transfer date.

issues.definition: When an appeal reviews a monetary decree requiring valuation at the transfer date and the record shows nearby transaction prices, the shares are valued at that date using the relevant market evidence.

issues.legal_issue: A non-joinder objection cannot be raised for the first time at the appellate stage when it was not taken in the courts below.
material_facts: The appellant argued that the suit was defective because the other partners of the firm had not been joined.
The appellant had not raised the objection in the courts below.
issues.conclusion: The non-joinder point could not be raised at that late stage.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the procedural principle that a point not taken in the courts below cannot be raised for the first time at a late stage of the appeal.

predicates.appeal_raises_nonjoinder_objection: A party raises an objection in an appeal that necessary parties were not joined.
predicates.objection_not_raised_below: The party did not raise the non-joinder objection in the courts below.

issues.definition: A non-joinder objection raised in an appeal cannot be considered when the party did not raise it in the courts below.
